title: Associated graded rings determine the dimension of a Noetherian local ring
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak n)$ and $(T,\mathfrak p)$ be commutative Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I\subseteq\mathfrak n$ and $J\subseteq\mathfrak p$ be ideals. Form the nonnegatively graded rings
$$\operatorname{gr}_I(R)=\bigoplus_{q\ge0}I^q/I^{q+1},\qquad \operatorname{gr}_J(T)=\bigoplus_{q\ge0}J^q/J^{q+1},$$
with multiplication induced by ideal multiplication and degree-zero parts $R/I$ and $T/J$. If these are isomorphic as graded rings, then $\dim R=\dim T$, where dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Zero ideals are allowed; the ideals need not be primary for the maximal ideals.

source.place: Expose III Corollary 5.4(i) and its proof, pp.42--43: the dimension at a point of the closed subscheme equals the dimension at the zero section of its normal cone (Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, Theorem 15.9, as cited there). This is its local-ring formulation for arbitrary ideals contained in the maximal ideals, used for each boundary intersection in the final paragraph of III Proposition 6.2, pp.44--45.

proof.text: We prove the comparison for an arbitrary pair $(R,\mathfrak n),I$ in the statement. Put $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R$ and $\mathfrak m=(\mathfrak n/I)\oplus\bigoplus_{q>0}G_q$, so $G/\mathfrak m=R/\mathfrak n$. In the Laurent polynomial ring (finite sums with convolution multiplication), put $E=R[t,I/t]$. If $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_s)$, then $E$ is generated over $R$ by $t,a_1/t,\ldots,a_s/t$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes it Noetherian. Its coefficient at $t^{-q}$ lies in $I^q$ for $q>0$, and its coefficients at nonnegative powers are arbitrary. The map $E\to R/\mathfrak n$ taking the constant coefficient modulo $\mathfrak n$ is multiplicative: every cross term of total exponent zero and nonzero exponents has a factor in $I\subseteq\mathfrak n$. Its kernel $M$ consists of Laurent sums whose constant coefficient is in $\mathfrak n$. Thus $M$ is maximal and $t\in M$. Put $A=E_M$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. This is Noetherian: an ideal in $A$ is generated by the images of finite generators of its contraction to $E$, since every denominator is a unit. Multiplication by $t$ on $E$ is injective by the shift of Laurent coefficients. It remains injective on $A$: if $t(b/s)=0$, some $u\notin M$ has $utb=0$, hence $ub=0$. Therefore $t/1$ is a nonzerodivisor in the maximal ideal of $A$.

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension], $d=\dim R$ is a finite nonnegative integer. There is a chain $P_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq P_d=\mathfrak n$ of length $d$: the finite integer supremum of attainable chain lengths is attained, and a longest chain must end at the unique maximal ideal. For a prime $P\subseteq R$, let $P^*$ be the kernel of $E	o(R/P)[t,t^{-1}]$. This is prime because the target is a domain and the kernel is proper; explicitly its elements have every Laurent coefficient in $P$. Thus $P_0^*\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq P_d^*$, with strictness detected by constant coefficients. Each $P_i^*$ lies in $M$. Moreover $P_d^*\subsetneq M$ because $t\in M$ has coefficient $1
otin\mathfrak n$. This gives a chain of length $d+1$ in $A$: extension and contraction preserve these primes and their strict inclusions. Explicitly, if $sb\in P_i^*$ and $s
otin M$, primality and $s
otin P_i^*$ imply $b\in P_i^*$, which verifies contraction. Hence $d+1\leq\dim A$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-laurent-subalgebra-dimension-bound] to the finite type $R$-subalgebra $E\subseteq R[t,t^{-1}]$ from step 1. It gives $\dim E\leq d+1$. Contracting a chain of primes of $E_M$ to $E$ preserves strictness (the fraction argument in step 2), so $\dim A\leq\dim E\leq d+1$. Together with step 2 this gives $\dim A=d+1$.

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-rees-associated-graded-chart] to identify $G\cong E/(t)$ by the isomorphism $e$ with $e([a]_q)=[a t^{-q}]$. The constant coefficient of $tb$ is the coefficient of $b$ at $t^{-1}$, which lies in $I\subseteq\mathfrak n$, so $(t)\subseteq M$ and $\bar M=M/(t)$ is a prime ideal of $E/(t)$ whose inverse image in $E$ is $M$. Under $e$ the inverse image of $\bar M$ is exactly $\mathfrak m$: a homogeneous class $[a]_q$ with $q>0$ goes to a sum with constant coefficient $0$, and $[a]_0$ goes to the constant $a$, which lies in $M$ iff $a\in\mathfrak n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] to the ring $E$, the ideal $(t)$ and the prime $\bar M$: the map $b/s\mapsto\bar b/\bar s$ is an isomorphism $A/(t/1)A=E_M/(t)E_M\cong(E/(t))_{\bar M}$. Since $e$ carries $G\setminus\mathfrak m$ onto $(E/(t))\setminus\bar M$, it induces $G_{\mathfrak m}\cong(E/(t))_{\bar M}$ by $a/s\mapsto e(a)/e(s)$, with inverse given by $e^{-1}$ in the same way; hence $A/(t/1)A\cong G_{\mathfrak m}$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] applies to the Noetherian local ring $A$ and the nonzerodivisor $t/1$ in its maximal ideal (step 1), giving $\dim(G_{\mathfrak m})+1=\dim A=d+1$ by step 3. Thus $\dim(G_{\mathfrak m})=d=\dim R$.

proof.text: Apply steps 1–4 also to $(T,\mathfrak p),J$, and write $H=\operatorname{gr}_J T$ and $\mathfrak l=(\mathfrak p/J)\oplus\bigoplus_{q>0}H_q$. The given graded isomorphism $e:G\cong H$ restricts to a ring isomorphism $R/I\cong T/J$. These rings are local: ideals maximal in a quotient correspond to maximal ideals of the original ring containing the quotient ideal, hence their unique maximal ideals are $\mathfrak n/I$ and $\mathfrak p/J$. Thus $e$ carries $\mathfrak m$ onto $\mathfrak l$, since it preserves degrees. It induces $G_{\mathfrak m}\cong H_{\mathfrak l}$ by $a/s\mapsto e(a)/e(s)$, with inverse from $e^{-1}$. Inverse image under this ring isomorphism is an inclusion-preserving bijection of prime ideals, so their Krull dimensions agree. Consequently $\dim R=\dim(G_{\mathfrak m})=\dim(H_{\mathfrak l})=\dim T$.
